headline: EPR Applications Specialist | Clinical Application Build, Workflow Redesign and Testing | MBBS-Trained Physician
summary: MBBS-trained physician with four years at Greenway Health, a US EHR company, where I took close to 200 client practices through discovery, workflow documentation, configuration, testing and go-live. I sat on the Patient Safety and Functional Advisory Committees, triaging defects and safety issues through release, and I turned clinician pain points into change requests that product teams shipped. Before that I worked in a Level 1 trauma ED and a COVID ICU, so ordering, results and documentation workflows are familiar to me from the bedside. My build work so far has been ambulatory and vendor-side, not a hospital EPR.
greenway_bullets: Ran EHR implementations for close to 200 client practices: discovery, documenting current and future-state clinical workflows, configuring practice-specific workflows and widgets, testing and go-live support.

Assessed requests for workflow and content changes, weighed the impact on clinicians and other modules, and worked with product and engineering teams on the fix; many changes I shaped shipped to clients.
Triaged defects and patient safety issues from detection through stage-gate release as a member of the Patient Safety Committee, Functional Advisory Committee and Clinical Content Team.
Trained 200+ end users, including providers, nurse practitioners, nurses and medical assistants, and supported them through stabilization.
Clinical lead for a new AI-first EHR from Aug 2025: provider personas, workflow mapping across the visit, and React prototypes before engineering handoff.
Reviewed clinical literature for EHR content and presented workflows to clients and at the Greenway Engage provider conference (50 attendees).
skills: clinical workflow documentation and redesign, configuration, test scripts and testing, change and enhancement requests, impact assessment, defect triage, go-live and stabilization support
patient safety review, stage-gate release, end-user training, clinician engagement, issue logs and status updates
emergency, ICU and ambulatory workflows (ordering, results, documentation); Microsoft Office; AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini), React, GitHub
thesis_html: An EPR build is safe when it matches how clinicians actually order, chart and read results.
why_fit: Workflow documentation, configuration and testing for each practice.
Triaged defects and safety issues through stage-gate release.
Senior resident in a Level 1 trauma ED and registrar in a COVID ICU.
